class.name: NetwConnectHandle
class.brief_description: The connect plane of one session, gathered onto one object.
class.description: A client over the [code]endpoint_*[/code], [code]transport_*[/code], [code]discovery_*[/code] and [code]peer_*[/code] families on [NetwMultiplayer], reached as [method Netw.connection] from any [Node]. Every member forwards to a flat verb, and the flat verb is the stable spelling: this repository's own suites, examples and browser call [NetwMultiplayer] directly, and a game reaches for this when it would rather hold the plane as one object. [codeblock] var c := Netw.connection(self) c.endpoint_add(ENetMultiplayerPeer, "203.0.113.42:21253") var ticket := c.create_peer( ENetMultiplayerPeer, NetwMultiplayer.TRANSPORT_MODE_CLIENT, "203.0.113.42:21253", {}, take_the_peer) [/codeblock] An endpoint is addressed by the pair it actually is, a transport and an address, never by a handle a caller must hold onto: every method on this axis takes a transport named any way [method transport] accepts (the peer class itself, a [Script], a [StringName], a live peer, or a handle already in hand) together with an address, and returns a snapshot [Dictionary] rather than a resource. The session still keys a row by [RID] internally, because it is the one thing here that outlives a file and a listing republish, but that [RID] never crosses onto this view. An endpoint snapshot carries [code]peer_class[/code], [code]address[/code], [code]display_name[/code], [code]status[/code], [code]info[/code], [code]is_caller_added[/code], [code]is_available[/code] and [code]is_observed[/code]. A transport snapshot carries [code]peer_class[/code], [code]display_name[/code], [code]address_label[/code], [code]address_placeholder[/code], [code]address_help[/code], [code]capabilities[/code], [code]host_settings[/code] and [code]client_settings[/code]. An empty [Dictionary] means absent, everywhere on this object. [b]This view holds no connection attempt state, and it never brings a session up.[/b] A session comes online the ordinary Godot way, by assigning a [MultiplayerPeer] to [member MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer]. [method create_peer] is here for the peer a provider rather than the game knows how to build, and it returns that one operation through the callables it was handed: the outcome reaches [code]completed[/code], each named step reaches [code]progress[/code], and [method cancel_peer_creation] withdraws exactly that ticket. What the SESSION is doing is read from the session, through [signal NetwMultiplayer.session_state_changed] and [signal NetwMultiplayer.session_entered].

method.name: cancel_peer_creation
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.transport_cancel_peer_creation] for the ticket [method create_peer] returned. The request settles with one [code](null, ERR_SKIP, "")[/code] callback and no peer is offered. A ticket that already completed, or one this session never created, is a no-op, so a view may cancel unconditionally before starting the next creation. The caller's own [Callable] is not what names the work: two creations sharing one bound [Callable] would be ambiguous, and the ticket never is.

diagnostics
method.description: What the session knows about its connection to [param peer_id], empty when it holds nothing for that peer.

method.name: endpoint
method.description: The snapshot for the endpoint [param transport] and [param address] name, empty when this session holds no such row. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴peer_class StringName ENetMultiplayerPeer, or a game's own ┃ transport ┠╴address String "203.0.113.42:21253" ┠╴display_name String what a server browser draws in the row ┠╴status int a MultiplayerPeer.ConnectionStatus value ┠╴info NetwServerInfo what this row last advertised, or null ┠╴is_caller_added bool true when this session's own endpoint_add ┃ added the row ┠╴is_available bool false while a probe is outstanding ┖╴is_observed bool true once a probe has reported back [/codeblock]

method.name: endpoint_add
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.endpoint_add]. Returns [code]true[/code] once the row exists, [code]false[/code] when [param transport] names nothing this build carries.

method.name: endpoint_probe
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.endpoint_probe] for the endpoint [param transport] and [param address] name, returning through [signal endpoint_updated].

method.name: endpoint_refresh
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.endpoint_refresh]: re-probes every known endpoint and reports each result through [signal endpoint_updated]. Discovery has its own lifetime, separate from the connection. A query opened here is torn down when the session is disposed or the provider behind it is withdrawn, and that teardown releases the query alone: it never closes the assigned peer, and never abandons a lobby the session is already in. A browser may therefore refresh, close, or be freed at any moment, including after the match it found has started, and the match outlives it.

method.name: endpoint_remove
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.endpoint_remove] for the endpoint [param transport] and [param address] name.

method.name: endpoint_set_display_name
method.description: Renames the endpoint [param transport] and [param address] name. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK written ┠╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED this view has no session ┖╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST no such row exists [/codeblock]

method.name: join_schema
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.session_get_join_schema], the wire parameters a Join form draws. [codeblock lang=text] Array[Dictionary] ┖╴entry ┠╴name String the argument's name ┠╴type int a Variant.Type value ┠╴class_name StringName empty for every type this build resolves ┖╴default Variant the value a Join form pre-fills, or null [/codeblock]

method.name: register_transport
method.description: Registers a [NetwTransport] subclass with the session this view sees, so its peer class joins [method transports] and can be named anywhere a transport is. [code]true[/code] when the session took it. [method NetwMultiplayer.transport_register] is the same operation and carries the ownership law: the registration belongs to the session and is released with it, a peer class is unique within a session, and the stock transports need no registration at all. Registering the same [param type] twice is not an error and changes nothing, so a scene that re-enters the tree may call this again. A [i]different[/i] script for a peer class this session already registers returns [code]false[/code] with a logged reason: call [method unregister_transport] first. [codeblock] func _ready() -> void: var c := Netw.connection(self) if c.register_transport(MyRelayTransport): c.create_peer( MyRelayTransport, NetwMultiplayer.TRANSPORT_MODE_HOST, "", {region = "eu"}, take_the_peer) [/codeblock]

method.name: transport
method.description: The snapshot for a transport named any way a caller has it: the peer class itself ([code]ENetMultiplayerPeer[/code]), a game transport's [Script], a [StringName], a live peer, or a handle already in hand. This is the view's whole job on this axis, so a game never types a class name and [NetwMultiplayer] can take nothing but the handle. Empty when this session holds no such transport. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴peer_class StringName the key this transport is registered under ┠╴display_name String what a Host or Add form's picker names it ┠╴address_label String what the address field is titled ┠╴address_placeholder String what the empty address field shows ┠╴address_help String the sentence under the address field ┠╴capabilities int a NetwMultiplayer.TransportCapability ┃ flag combination ┠╴host_settings Dictionary the fields a host form asks for, named ┃ by this transport alone ┖╴client_settings Dictionary the fields a join form asks for, which overlap the host ones by however much the two modes share [/codeblock] [codeblock] var c := Netw.connection(self) var enet := c.transport(ENetMultiplayerPeer) prints(enet["display_name"], enet["address_placeholder"]) [/codeblock]

method.name: transports
method.description: Every transport this session can reach, as transport snapshots shaped like [method transport] returns.

method.name: unregister_transport
method.description: Withdraws a registration [method register_transport] made, naming it the way every verb on this view names a transport: the [Script] that was registered, its peer class as a [StringName], or a live peer of that class. [code]true[/code] when this session held it, [code]false[/code] for anything it did not register, a stock transport included. [b]It is not a disconnect.[/b] A peer this transport already handed over stays assigned, exactly as [method NetwMultiplayer.transport_unregister] describes. What ends is unfinished work: a build still in flight settles with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE], and the transport's browsing closes, so its rows stop arriving on [signal endpoint_added].

members.member: Every row this session knows how to reach, as endpoint snapshots. Equivalent to [method endpoints].
[method NetwMultiplayer.peer_join_address]: the address another player would use to reach this session.

signal.name: endpoint_added
signal.description: [signal NetwMultiplayer.endpoint_added], relayed by the pair it names. A row already known announces nothing.

signal.name: endpoint_removed
signal.description: [signal NetwMultiplayer.endpoint_removed], relayed by the pair it named.

signal.name: endpoint_updated
signal.description: [signal NetwMultiplayer.endpoint_updated], relayed by the pair it names. What changed is read back through [method endpoint].

signal.name: join_failed
signal.description:
This peer's own join was rejected, locally or by the server, and no player was seated for it. [param reason] is the server's own words where the rejection came from one, and [param error] is why. A rejection is not a disconnect notice: it is the result to the join this peer asked for, so a game shows it where it asked, beside its username field rather than in a lobby-lost banner. A server rejects when the handler declared through [method Netw.configure_join] is unavailable, when the join carried no arguments a declared handler needs, or when that handler returned something that is not a placement. [codeblock] func _ready() -> void: Netw.connection(self).join_failed.connect(show_refusal)
func show_refusal(_error: int, reason: String) -> void: status.text = reason [/codeblock]
